title: School bond passage and district spending: Cellini, Ferreira and Rothstein (2010)
estimand: Intent-to-treat effect of narrowly passing a school-district general-obligation bond measure on spending per pupil three years later (2000s dollars per pupil); each panel is a different outcome.
estimate_label: Effect of passage on spending per pupil, year 3 ($)

options.label: Capital outlays per pupil
options.justification: CFR Table IV Panel A (baseline): bond revenue funds capital projects.

options.label: Instructional spending per pupil (placebo)
options.justification: CFR Table IV Panel A; bond revenue cannot legally fund instruction, so a jump would signal a problem with the design.

options.label: Cubic (CFR)
options.justification: CFR baseline: cubic in vote share for each relative year, with threshold-regime terms.

options.label: Quadratic
options.justification: CFR Table VI varies the polynomial order; Gelman and Imbens (2019) caution against high-order global polynomials.

options.label: Linear
options.justification: Lowest-order global control; natural with narrow windows.

options.label: Linear, separate slopes each side
options.justification: Standard local-linear RD: the slope in the vote margin may differ above and below the threshold.

options.label: All measures (CFR)
options.justification: CFR baseline: global polynomial over all measures, equal weights.

options.label: Within 20 points, uniform
options.justification: Local estimation: only measures whose vote share is within 20 points of the required share; equal weights within the window.

options.label: Within 20 points, triangular
options.justification: Local estimation: only measures whose vote share is within 20 points of the required share; triangular weights fall linearly to zero at the window edge.

options.label: Within 10 points, uniform
options.justification: Local estimation: only measures whose vote share is within 10 points of the required share; equal weights within the window.

options.label: Within 10 points, triangular
options.justification: Local estimation: only measures whose vote share is within 10 points of the required share; triangular weights fall linearly to zero at the window edge.

options.label: Within 5 points, uniform
options.justification: Local estimation: only measures whose vote share is within 5 points of the required share; equal weights within the window.

options.label: Within 5 points, triangular
options.justification: Local estimation: only measures whose vote share is within 5 points of the required share; triangular weights fall linearly to zero at the window edge.

options.label: Drop measures within 1 point
options.justification: Guards against sorting, recounts or misrecorded vote shares at the threshold.

options.label: Both thresholds (CFR)
options.justification: CFR pool the two-thirds and 55 percent thresholds.

options.label: Two-thirds measures only
options.justification: One threshold and one voting rule; pooling cutoffs is a design choice (Hsu and Shen 2024).

reference.source: Cellini, Ferreira and Rothstein (2010), Quarterly Journal of Economics 125(1), Table IV, Panel A (capital outlays, year 3); authors' log fiscaltab_rf.log reports 1121.41 (243.79), N = 6,970

notes: Window, kernel, donut and threshold choices refer to the vote margin of the measure that defines each stack. fixest drops 24 fixed-effect singletons that Stata's areg keeps (N = 6,946 against 6,970); the point estimate is unchanged. Standard errors treat measure effects as nested in district clusters, so they are smaller than areg's (222.6 against 243.8).
